subject: Post-demo: clarify deployment lane & hosted quick-access plan
body:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Sara Albers <sara@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: clarify deployment lane & hosted quick-access plan

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying items so we can lock the right onboarding lane (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap: Finlytics liked the latency profile and prefix caching demo. Your team wants predictable per-request latency for customer-facing scoring (SLA ~ 200ms p95 for 512-token avg), and you'd like to avoid heavy operational overhead for now.

Open questions from my side:
- Production target: is the SLA request (200ms p95) for all traffic or only premium customers?
- Peak profile: can you confirm the 6-hour daily window numbers in the CSV (attached) — currently listed as 1.8k req/min, burst to 4k for 10 minutes.
- Data residency: all customer data must remain in US regions; any extra requirements (e.g., dedicated tenancy, private peering)?
- Integration preference: do you want us to provision a Hosted sandbox first and later move to Dedicated if throughput/cost needs change?

For Hosted-specific items I recommend for the quickstart:
1) Sandbox endpoint (hosted) with a dedicated sandbox key (30-day access)
2) Rate caps mapped to two endpoints: scoring (high-volume) and experiments (low-volume); we'll propose endpoint token caps so you can enforce internal SLAs
3) KV prefix caching enabled at the edge for scoring endpoints
4) Optional canary routing to a dedicated pool if/when you move to Dedicated capacity

Next actions I propose:
- Sara: confirm the SLA scope (premium-only vs all traffic) and approve the sandbox request (we'll need a list of 2 engineers to receive keys).
- Finlytics Ops: confirm the traffic CSV numbers or send updated traffic curves.
- Redwood: Ben and Karthik will prepare a hosted quickstart playbook (endpoints + rate plan + short checklist) and a cost sketch comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for the profile you provided.

If this plan looks good I'll kick off the sandbox provisioning today and share the quickstart playbook by tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finlytics-mvp-traffic-snapshot.csv (text/csv), redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

---

On Tue, 12 May 2026 at 17:03 Sara Albers <sara@finlytics.ai> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
>
> Thanks — good summary. A few answers inline:
>
> - SLA scope: premium customers only (about 15% of calls currently).
> - Traffic: the CSV is accurate for current beta traffic; we expect a 2x growth in 3 months after GA but that can be modelled separately.
> - Data residency: US-only is sufficient for now, no HSM requirement in the initial phase.
> - Engineers: please send keys to me and to devops@finlytics.ai (two people: me and Javier Morales).
>
> We'd like the Hosted sandbox first — lower ops burden and faster time-to-value. How long to get the sandbox up? Also curious about token-level billing visibility during the trial.
>
> Best,
> Sara
> Head of Product, Finlytics
>
>
---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Sara Albers <sara@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify deployment lane & hosted quick-access plan

Sara — great to hear Hosted is the preferred first step. A few concrete notes on the quickstart and the hosted constraints so expectations are clear: 

- Sandbox provisioning: 24 hours business time once we have the engineer list and a signed sandbox terms doc (I can attach the DocuSign link).
- Endpoints: we'll create 2 API routes for you: /v1/scoring (high QPS) and /v1/experiments (low QPS). Each route maps to token-based caps and a separate API key for easier throttling and cost allocation.
- Default rate caps for your profile: scoring -> 2000 req/min (soft), burst to 4000 for 10 minutes (hard); experiments -> 100 req/min. These are editable after we see traffic.
- Latency: Hosted p95 targets for 512 tokens on our curated best-fit model should be ~150-220ms depending on concurrency; we'll instrument token-level timing and share live metrics in the Console.
- Billing visibility: the Console provides token breakdown per API key and per endpoint; we'll also share a short CSV export for the pilot cadence.
- Cache: prefix/KV caching enabled by default on the scoring endpoint; you can tune TTL and prefixing in the route config.

I'll prepare the quickstart playbook (endpoints + keys + sample curl and SDK snippets) and the DocuSign sandbox form. If you want, Karthik can add suggested endpoint ceiling numbers tuned to your growth forecast (2x in 3 months).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Sara Albers <sara@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify deployment lane & hosted quick-access plan

Perfect — thanks Sara and Ben. Sara: I'll trigger the sandbox provisioning once you confirm the two engineer emails (sara@finlytics.ai, ops@finlytics.ai) and sign the DocuSign. Ben — please attach the DocuSign link and the playbook PDF to the HubSpot deal so Sara's team can access them. Karthik — if you can include a brief cost delta (monthly estimate) for moving from Hosted to Dedicated at 2x load, that will close the loop for their finance team.

I'll set a 30-minute follow-up on Tue May 19 to walk through the playbook and sample calls. Proposed times: 10am PT or 2pm PT — which works for you, Sara?

Thanks,
Grace
